transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Ethan Park (Starlit Head of ML); Rina Kaur (Platform Eng); Liam O'Connor (CTO)
Links shared: Redwood reserved SKU deck (drive link), benchmark spreadsheet (link), security brief (link)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, brevity may miss details): Starlit is evaluating a Dedicated reservation with warm-pools for bursty inference across image and text models. Key concerns: isolation between tenants, prewarm cost, fallback to hosted during large spikes, and KMS/SSO for Private. Action: Redwood to send pricing + warm-pool runbook, schedule follow-up technical deep dive.

Topics: reserved capacity options, warm-pool prewarming, KV cache warm strategies, isolation (node vs tenant), burst fallback, model quantization tradeoffs, compliance (SOC2, KMS), expected scaling patterns.

Transcript:
[15:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll quickly run through agenda — reserved capacity, warm pools, failover patterns — and then Diego can walk through the technical options, is that good?
[15:08] Ethan (Starlit): yep that sounds great, thanks Maya. Quick context from us: we run a multimodal assistant, bursty traffic around product releases, and we saw a 6x spike earlier this month which killed our self-hosted autoscaler.
[15:22] Rina (Starlit): and we need isolation between our internal traffic and customer tenants because of compliance, plus we want guaranteed baseline throughput during business hours.
[15:31] Diego (Redwood): totally, yep. So Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved node pools — you can pick node types (A100/H100) and define warm-pool sizes. Warm-pool is basically prewarmed VMs/containers with KV cache primed for common prefixes. We do continuous batching but you can set latency SLOs.
[15:47] Liam (Starlit): when you say warm-pool, are we paying for that idle capacity all the time? that's my main worry.
[15:53] Maya (Redwood): good question. There are a few levers: reserved vs prewarm-on-demand. Reserved warm-pools are part of your commit (cheaper unit cost), on-demand prewarm can be set to spin up quickly but costs more; we also offer burst credits for short-term spikes.
[16:10] Ethan (Starlit): can you elaborate on burst credits and fallback to Redwood Hosted? we have a hybrid rule that if our cluster can't serve within 200ms we failover to a hosted endpoint — but worried about the data residency and PII.
[16:24] Diego (Redwood): fallback to Hosted is supported, you can configure routing policies to only send non-sensitive requests. For PII we recommend VPC peering + tokenization before hitting hosted endpoints; otherwise Private deployments with KMS are the path.
[16:38] Rina (Starlit): is KMS supported in Private and Dedicated? We need HSM integrations and key rotation audit logs for SOC2.
[16:45] Diego (Redwood): yes, Dedicated + Private integrate with customer KMS/HSM; we log key usage in audit trails. Small note: audit retention packages are an add-on.
[16:55] Ethan (Starlit): what metrics should we send you to size the warm-pool? we can export p95 token/sec, p99 latency, and session length.
[17:03] Maya (Redwood): perfect. Prefer a 7-day sampled trace with timestamps, tokens per call, and concurrency windows. Diego: how do we turn that into a prewarm sizing?
[17:12] Diego (Redwood): we look at percentile concurrency and typical sequence lengths. For example, if p95 concurrency is 120 and average seq is 1k tokens, we suggest a baseline pool that covers p50-p75 and burst credits for p90-p99. Also consider mixed GPU SKUs: cheaper 8-bit quantized variants for background workloads.
[17:34] Liam (Starlit): mixed GPUs meaning you can have different node types in the same pool? does that complicate routing?
[17:40] Diego (Redwood): we do model routing by compatibility. If you pin a model variant to a pool, Redwood routes requests to compatible nodes. There's some overhead but runtime does kernel selection; routing policy can prefer cheaper nodes for non-latency sensitive requests.
[17:57] Rina (Starlit): about isolation: do you do tenant-level cgroups, or full node isolation? we want cryptographic separation between workloads.
[18:06] Diego (Redwood): Dedicated supports full-node isolation (single-tenant nodes) as well as tenant isolation via cgroups on shared nodes. For regulated workloads we recommend single-tenant nodes. There's a cost differential — single-tenant nodes are part of a premium isolation SKU.
[18:24] Ethan (Starlit): ok, so if we reserve a pool of single-tenant nodes for customer-sensitive calls and a shared-pool for internal telemetry, how does failover work between them? we don't want spikes to starve the customer-sensitive pool.
[18:36] Maya (Redwood): you can set strict QoS and priority routing. High-priority routes consume only from the single-tenant pool; lower-priority traffic can be queued or failover to hosted. You can also define autoscale policies with minimums per pool.
[18:51] Liam (Starlit): what about prewarming KV cache — can you persist KV cache between restarts or do we need to rebuild on each startup?
[18:58] Diego (Redwood): we persist checkpoints for common prefixes and you can seed the cache via warm-up scripts. The runbook Diego will share describes pattern: sample prompts -> synthesize prefixes -> seed cache during warm-pool prewarm.
[19:12] Rina (Starlit): any differences in warm-up time between A100 and H100?
[19:16] Diego (Redwood): H100s are faster to populate due to higher memory bandwidth but cost more. For quantized variants the warm time is slightly lower.
[19:26] Ethan (Starlit): pricing: do you charge per-token on Dedicated or per-hour for reserved nodes? we have a current cost model based on per-inference compute time.
[19:34] Maya (Redwood): reserved Dedicated is primarily commit (per-node/hour) with additional per-token billing optional for hosted burst or extra usage beyond commit. We'll send a matrix with per-node/hour, prewarm storage fees, and burst credit rates.
[19:48] Rina (Starlit): how do you handle model version rollouts across a pool? do you support canaries?
[19:52] Diego (Redwood): yes, rollouts are first-class: canary pools, traffic split, A/B testing. We also do automatic fallback to a pinned stable variant if the canary exceeds error thresholds.
[20:03] Ethan (Starlit): does Redwood provide telemetry hooks for our tracing system? we use open telemetry with internal dashboards.
[20:09] Diego (Redwood): yup, we emit traces and per-token latency breakdowns and you can plumb them into your OTEL collector. We'll include tracing hooks in the runbook.
[20:18] [short crosstalk]
[20:22] Liam (Starlit): security/compliance aside, what are realistic expectations for failure modes? like, say a provider patch causes hot restarts — do you auto-failover?
[20:30] Diego (Redwood): we have rolling updates with drain and warm-pool prewarming to avoid cold starts. For catastrophic node outage we route to other pools or hosted fallback if policy allows; we also support cross-region replication for DR.
[20:46] Ethan (Starlit): cross-region replication — is stateful KV cache replicated?
[20:50] Diego (Redwood): KV cache checkpointing can be replicated to a secondary region but there's a warm-up window; we advise keeping smaller warm-pools in each region if you need tight RTO.
[21:05] Maya (Redwood): quick product note: Optimize recommendations can analyze your traffic and suggest quantization and batch sizes — that often reduces prewarm cost.
[21:15] Rina (Starlit): great — can we run a cost simulation? like what does 2x baseline + 6x spike look like for 24 hours?
[21:22] Maya (Redwood): yes, Redwood will run a cost sim given the trace; please send the 7-day trace and we'll return a simulation matrix.
[21:30] [short pause]
[21:33] Ethan (Starlit): a couple edge questions: 1) can we bring our own model artifacts with private weights to Dedicated? 2) how does licensing work for commercial models?
[21:41] Diego (Redwood): BYO models are supported for Private and Dedicated; we help with onboarding and quantization. Licensing depends on model vendor — we provide guidance but customers manage license compliance.
[21:53] Liam (Starlit): anything we should watch out for when doing mixed workloads (text + image) on same pool?
[21:59] Diego (Redwood): image workloads have larger memory/latency profile; we recommend separate pools when image inference is heavy. If combined, ensure node selection matches the heaviest workload.
[22:12] Rina (Starlit): about networking — VPC, peering, egress auditing — do you support private endpoints with no public egress?
[22:20] Diego (Redwood): yes, Private + Dedicated can be deployed behind customer VPCs with no public egress; egress controls and flow logs are supported for audit.
[22:32] Ethan (Starlit): any surprises in onboarding time for Dedicated + Private? we have a regulatory deadline in Q3.
[22:37] Maya (Redwood): typical onboarding for Dedicated is 4-8 weeks depending on model onboarding and network config; Private/on-prem can take longer (8-12 weeks). We'll map milestones in a project plan.
[22:49] Liam (Starlit): what's the SLA for prewarmed latency?
[22:52] Diego (Redwood): we can commit to p95 latency targets per model in the SLA for Dedicated, depends on node type and model checkpoint.
[23:03] Rina (Starlit): okay one last technical — how do you handle KV cache invalidation when models are updated?
[23:09] Diego (Redwood): we version caches per model variant; when you rollout a new variant we either rebuild caches or serve fallback to old variant for cache-missing prefixes. Rebuild time can be estimated in the runbook.
[23:21] Maya (Redwood): quick recap and next steps: Redwood to send reserved pricing matrix, warm-pool runbook, and cost simulation template. Schedule deep dive (Rina + Diego) for 2026-05-21. Starlit to send traffic trace by 2026-05-17.
[23:36] Ethan (Starlit): sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[23:40] Liam (Starlit): thanks, this was helpful.
[23:43] Maya (Redwood): thanks all, will follow up with summary and links.
[23:47] [meeting ends]
